governing_plan_context.finding: Official2014 Route66 Action Plan delivery has adoption cover: Council2014-11-03, Mayor2014-11-24; RankII15-mile corridor framework for preservation/redevelopment, heritage, economic investment and infrastructure. This is the antecedent the2017 draft proposed to amend, not a later adoption of that draft.

Current City Comp Plan page identifies Rank1 policy,2017/2024/2025 editions and application-date applicability. This broad citywide policy framework is not the237-page GreaterCentral study or its supporting engineering/fiscal work.

Current City IDO page provides adopted ordinance/effective-date history and governing zoning for applications; currentMay6,2026 edition followsO-26-10. Station-area draft suggested actions/projections do not substitute for those adopted regulations.

FY19 approved budget GreaterCentral objective supports partnership goals, technical working groups and translating priorities into an action plan for Council consideration. It shows continuation of initiative, not completed adoption or wholesale supersession of report.

comparison: The2014 plan is an adopted corridor-wide framework; Comp Plan/IDO govern policy and development regulations. The2017/2018 documents offer station-specific scenarios, barrier/action matrices and consultant assumptions and explicitly remain potential/nonmandatory recommendations. These distinct functions explain why the current regulations are not substitutes for the historical report as a public-information source.
legal_limit: No claim that lack of a recovered enactment proves no enactment existed. No adoption inferred from appropriation, procurement or a document being City-delivered.
